fields.title: South Korea Proof of Funds for Indian Students: KRW 20 Million Rule
fields.summary: How much money to show for a South Korea D-2 student visa: the Ministry of Justice standard of KRW 20 million or KRW 16 million, what universities ask for and how to show it.
fields.seo_title: South Korea Proof of Funds: KRW 20 Million Visa Rule
fields.meta_description: South Korea proof of funds for a D-2 student visa: KRW 20 million (capital area) or KRW 16 million, what KAIST and Korea University ask for and how to show it.
fields.body_md:
## The short answer

Korea wants to see that you can pay one year of tuition and living costs. This is the money you show for your **D-2 student visa**.

- **Ministry of Justice standard:** **KRW 20 million** (**₹13.89 lakh**) for a university in the Seoul capital area. **KRW 16 million** (**₹11.11 lakh**) for a university elsewhere.
- **Your university sets its own figure.** KAIST says to show **USD 16,000** (**₹14.87 lakh**). The Korea University Global MBA asked for **USD 30,000** (**₹27.87 lakh**) in its Fall 2026 cycle.
- **Who holds the money:** your own account or your parents' account. If you use your parents' account, you also give papers that prove the family link.
- **Not a budget:** this is the minimum for the visa. Our [cost of living guide](/study-abroad/study-in/south-korea/south-korea-cost-of-living) shows what students spend each month.

Rupee amounts use **₹0.0694 per Korean won**. We built that rate from two official rates for 27 November 2026. One is the RBI rate of ₹92.91 per US dollar. The other is the Bank of Korea close of ₩1,337.9 per US dollar. Rates move every day. Your bank will charge its own rate, so treat the rupee figures as a guide.

## What the Ministry of Justice says

On 5 February 2026 the Ministry of Justice published a press release about a pilot for junior colleges. It states the standing rule in a footnote: "유학(D-2) 비자발급시 재정요건 : 수도권 소재 대학 2,000만원, 지방대학 1,600만원". In English, the D-2 financial requirement is **KRW 20 million** for a university in the capital area. It is **KRW 16 million** for a provincial university.

"Capital area" means the metropolitan area around Seoul. The press release does not list the cities. Ask your university which group it is in.

You may see older figures online: **USD 20,000** for a degree and **USD 18,000** at provincial universities. Korea.net is the Government's official website. On 23 June 2023 it reported a change by the Ministry of Justice. The currency moved "from USD to KRW, with a lower amount required". The new rules took effect on 3 July 2023.

## What your university can ask for

The visa officer works from your admission letter and the cost of stay on it. Universities can also set their own figure. Here are two examples from official university pages:

| University | What it says | In rupees |
|---|---|---|
| KAIST | Plan for about **USD 16,000** a year if you are self-funded or parent-funded. Bank statements should show **USD 16,000** or more. | ₹14.87 lakh |
| Korea University Global MBA (Fall 2026 cycle) | A bank statement showing at least **USD 30,000** or the same amount in another currency. | ₹27.87 lakh |

KAIST's guide calls its figure the Ministry of Justice minimum. That does not match the won amount in the press release above. KAIST also says USD 16,000 covers tuition for two semesters and other costs for a year on campus. Its own budget below comes to more than that. Treat the university's number as the one you must meet, and ask the university to confirm.

## How to show the money

- Use a bank statement or balance certificate from your bank, in your name or your parents' name.
- Korea University asks for the statement in English. It must show the holder's name, balance, currency, issue date and validity period.
- The account must belong to the successful candidate or a parent. For a parent's account, Korea University asks for a **family relation certificate** in English. Another official paper that proves the link also works. Study in Korea lists it as "Documents Proving Family Relationship".
- A statement with a validity period must stay valid when you submit it. It must also stay valid when you apply for the visa. Korea University says so.
- With a scholarship, you show the difference between USD 30,000 and the scholarship. Korea University says so.

The New Delhi Embassy has general guidance for Indians applying on an invitation. It lists income tax returns for the last 2 years and bank statements for 6 months. The D-2 and D-4 checklist for your office decides the exact papers. See our [student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/south-korea-student-visa-guide).

## Worked example: KAIST without a scholarship

KAIST publishes its 2027 tuition and an average budget for a student living on campus.

| Item | Amount | In rupees |
|---|---|---|
| Tuition, 2 semesters at KRW 9,559,000 | **KRW 19,118,000** | ₹13.28 lakh |
| Other costs, 12 months on campus (KRW 5,350,000 for each 6 months) | **KRW 10,700,000** | ₹7.43 lakh |
| **Total for one year** | **KRW 29,818,000** | **₹20.71 lakh** |

KAIST mixes years: tuition is for 2027 and the budget is for 2026. It says students who live off campus should expect living costs to be 35% to 50% higher. KAIST also says its scholarship can cover full tuition. KAIST decides scholarships separately from admission. Do not plan on a scholarship until you hold the offer.

## Sources

Official pages, checked on 28 November 2026: [Ministry of Justice press release, 5 February 2026](https://www.immigration.go.kr/bbs/moj/182/490464/download.do), [Korea.net: student visa reform, 23 June 2023](https://www.korea.net/NewsFocus/policies/view?articleId=234525), [Study in Korea: Student Visa and Stay Status](https://www.studyinkorea.go.kr/en/plan/visaAndStay.do), [KAIST 2027 Fall International Graduate Admission guide](https://www.studyinkorea.go.kr/cmm/fms/FileDown.do?atchFileId=FILE_000000000483722&fileSn=1), [Korea University Business School: Global MBA admissions](https://biz.korea.ac.kr/eng/mba/globalMBA/admission), [Embassy of Korea in India](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/in-ko/brd/m_2803/view.do?page=1&seq=1301843), [RBI exchange rates](https://www.rbi.org.in/) and the [Bank of Korea ECOS statistics](https://ecos.bok.or.kr).

faq_json.q: How much money do I need to show for a South Korea student visa?
faq_json.a: The Ministry of Justice standard is KRW 20 million for a university in the capital area and KRW 16 million elsewhere, about ₹13.89 lakh and ₹11.11 lakh. Your university may ask for more.

faq_json.q: Is the Korea visa amount still USD 20,000?
faq_json.a: No. The Ministry of Justice changed the amount from US dollars to Korean won in July 2023, and lowered it. Some websites still quote the old dollar figures.

faq_json.q: Can my parents' bank account be used?
faq_json.a: Yes. Study in Korea lists parents' bank statements with papers that prove the family relationship. Korea University says the account can belong to a parent.

faq_json.q: Does KAIST ask for more than the visa minimum?
faq_json.a: KAIST says self-funded and parent-funded applicants must show a balance of USD 16,000 or more, about ₹14.87 lakh. A KAIST scholarship can cover full tuition, but it is decided separately from admission.

faq_json.q: What did the Korea University Global MBA ask for?
faq_json.a: In its Fall 2026 cycle it asked successful candidates for a bank statement with at least USD 30,000, about ₹27.87 lakh. A scholarship holder shows the difference between USD 30,000 and the scholarship.
